sources.note: Nothing. 'Elements phonologiques' pp.15-20 covers syllable (CV, CVC, syllabic nasal), consonants, vowels/palatalisation-labialisation prosodies, and sec. 5 'Les tons' (p.20): two level tones H/L, nominal tone schemes H-H, B-B, H-B (no lexical B-H), grammatical rising BH on last syllable; morpho-phonology pp.20ff. gives tone raising/lowering/assimilation rules. No mention of stress/accent d'intensite anywhere in the book (only 'accent' = acute diacritic for H tone).

sources.note: Nothing for Mafa; the reconstruction explicitly excludes 'tone or stress'. Mafa group sections (3.3.3, 5.3.5 pp.49, 116-118) treat vowel harmony/prosodies and state that Mafa 'has a published phonology', citing Barreteau & Le Bleis 1990.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel & Yves Le Bleis. 1984. Document de reference pour la standardisation de la langue mafa. Yaounde: MESRES / ISH / CREA. 22 pp. IRD Horizon fdi:20555 (also rescanned at dayimafa.net/images/PDF/).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 6 'Les tons' (p.15-16 of the typescript; scanned poor): 'Dans la langue mafa, chaque centre de syllabe (voyelle ou nasale syllabique) porte une hauteur musicale determinee.. chaque syllabe est caracterisee par un ton propre. Deux registres tonals sont observes: haut et bas'; H marked by an acute accent, L unmarked; tones have low functional load in nouns, higher in verbs; tone schemes listed for 1-3 syllable words.
